explication:
Overview

OwnPay is a self-hosted PHP payment-gateway automation platform. It provides hosted checkout, payment links, invoices, payment intents, refunds, multi-currency handling, REST APIs, webhooks, multi-brand isolation, and a double-entry ledger. The README describes support for 120+ gateway integrations and deployment behind a web server whose document root is public/.

Public entry points

  • public/index.php is the web front controller.
  • config/routes/web.php and config/routes/api.php organize browser, checkout, administrative, and JSON API routes.
  • HTTP-facing areas are represented by src/Controller, including admin, checkout, API, installation, page, and webhook controllers.
  • src/Controller/Webhook and src/Controller/Admin/GatewayWebhookController.php are the repository’s webhook-facing areas.

Core components

  • HTTP kernel and routing — src/Kernel.php: custom application bootstrapping, request/response handling, routing, dependency wiring, and middleware composition. The repository uses a custom core rather than a full-stack framework.
  • Payment application services — src/Service/Payment: implementation areas for payment, transaction, invoice, payment-link, refund, fee, currency, ledger, reconciliation, idempotency, and webhook operations.
  • Persistence and financial state — database/schema.sql: database schema and SQL migrations back the repositories in src/Repository. Persistent records include merchants, brands, customers, gateways, payment objects, transactions, ledger data, webhooks, settings, and audit information.
  • Gateway abstraction and integrations — src/Gateway: defines the gateway adapter boundary, bridges configured gateways, and processes inbound gateway events. Individual provider implementations live under modules/gateways, with one manifest and adapter area per provider.
  • Tenant and security boundaries — src/Middleware: request controls include authentication, sessions, permissions, CSRF, rate limiting, idempotency, domains, signatures, and security headers. src/Security contains validation, encryption, masking, and URL/security helpers; brand scoping is also represented by src/Repository/TenantScope.php.
  • Extension runtime — src/Plugin: plugin manifests, loading, installation, migration, sandboxing, capabilities, and registries provide the extension boundary. Add-ons are under modules/addons; themes are under modules/themes.
  • Presentation — src/View: Twig and plain-PHP rendering, theme resolution, plugin views, and themed responses support the admin UI, customer checkout, installation pages, and error pages. Templates are organized under templates.
  • Background operations — src/Cron: scheduled-job areas cover reconciliation, webhook retries, currency and DNS updates, SMS processing, balance verification, and system updates. Queue and cache implementations are provided under src/Queue and src/Cache.

Relationships

Merchants or their stores use the REST/API or browser-facing controllers to create payment objects. OwnPay’s payment services select configured gateway adapters and render branded checkout for customers. Customers interact with external payment providers; provider callbacks or webhooks return to the webhook controllers and gateway processing boundary. The payment domain then records transaction and ledger state and can notify the merchant through configured notification or webhook services.

Administrators and staff use the admin controllers and rendered views to manage brands, gateways, users, settings, plugins, and financial records. Gateway authors, add-on authors, and theme authors extend repository-owned interfaces through the module and plugin boundaries; their code remains separate from the core application.

External dependencies and state

Runtime deployment requires PHP 8.3+, MySQL/MariaDB, and provider-specific external gateway APIs. Redis is an available cache/queue technology alongside file-backed implementations. Writable storage and upload locations support runtime files, logs, cache, backups, and uploaded assets.
